title: Muffin — Providers & cache
description: Outbound provider traffic through http-cache. KNOWN BLIND SPOT: yfinance/finviz/FMP calls made INSIDE openbb-api do not pass through the proxy, so the rate-limit signal that matters most still comes from the Pipeline dashboard's failure panel.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Every request this serves is a provider call not made. Both ways the cache breaks are silent: `inactive=` defaults to 10 minutes and evicts by LAST ACCESS, and a cache key over proxy_buffer_size makes nginx stop caching while still answering correctly.

panels.title: Hit ratio by provider
panels.description: OpenFIGI and Alpha Vantage matter most: 25 requests a minute and 25 a DAY respectively.

panels.title: Response status by class
panels.description: Non-2xx only. A 4xx spike on a provider is usually a rate limit — and note nothing non-2xx is ever cached, deliberately: a cached 429 is poison.

panels.title: p95 latency by provider
panels.description: A cache HIT is served from disk, so a rising p95 usually means the hit ratio fell rather than that a provider got slower — read this with the panel above it.

panels.title: Bytes served: cache vs origin
panels.description: SEC XBRL companyfacts alone is ~3.6 MB per filer across 3,516 filers.

panels.title: http-cache on disk — bytes and entries
panels.description:
The http-cache volume ITSELF, from `muffin_http_cache_bytes`. It previously plotted `node_filesystem_size - node_filesystem_avail` for /mnt/data — the WHOLE FILESYSTEM — under a title claiming it was the cache. Measured 2026-08-28 that is 9.4 GB of which the cache is 0.6: **90% of it is muffin_supabase-db-data at 8.4 GB**. That is why it drifted DOWN from time to time — Postgres recycling WAL and vacuuming, nothing to do with a cache. For the host's disk see the Node dashboard.

ENTRIES IS PLOTTED BESIDE BYTES because bytes alone cannot distinguish a cache holding four enormous SEC companyfacts payloads from one holding forty thousand small OpenFIGI answers. A real fall in either is nginx's cache manager evicting — `proxy_cache_path` enforces `max_size` (8 GB) and `inactive=`, which evicts by LAST ACCESS, not by TTL.

panels.title: Provider requests leaving the cache — observed for direct providers, INFERRED for openbb
panels.description:
WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. For the seven DIRECT providers (sec, sec-data, sec-fts, openfigi, yahoo, alphavantage, tiingo) http-cache proxies straight to the external origin, so a non-HIT genuinely left the node — OBSERVED.

For `openbb:*` it is an INFERENCE. A miss forwards to openbb-api INSIDE the swarm, and openbb-api then calls yfinance/finviz/FMP itself without traversing this cache. The label comes from the `?provider=` parameter on the way in, so it counts requests that SHOULD cause an upstream call — not the call itself. It can differ: openbb may cache internally, a 12-symbol request may be one batched upstream call or twelve, and a 4xx may never reach the provider at all.

The panel was first titled 'requests that actually left the node', which is true for the direct providers and an overclaim for openbb — the same failure the `rows_estimate.*` naming exists to avoid. TRUE per-provider egress from openbb-api needs network-level counting (nftables/eBPF); a forward proxy will not do it, because aiohttp ignores *_PROXY unless trust_env=True and modern yfinance fetches through curl_cffi.

Only cache_status != HIT is drawn: a HIT makes no upstream call at all.

panels.title: Egress connections by host — observed, every container
panels.description:
EVERY EXTERNAL HOST THIS NODE CONNECTS TO, FOR EVERY CONTAINER, WITH NO PER-SERVICE CONFIG. The panel above it infers openbb's provider from a query parameter; this OBSERVES the connection itself, and covers what http-cache cannot see at all — openbb-api's own calls to yfinance, firecrawl's scraping, the agent's LLM calls, opensandbox.

HOW: every HTTPS connection opens with a TLS ClientHello carrying `server_name` in PLAINTEXT. No decryption, no CA, no MITM — the client states which host it wants. The BPF filter runs IN THE KERNEL (25 instructions, measured) so only ClientHello packets reach userspace.

IT COUNTS CONNECTIONS, NOT REQUESTS. HTTP keep-alive reuses one connection for many requests, so this is an undercount of unknown factor — demonstrated while building it, when a driven openbb call produced no new ClientHello because the connection already existed. The metric is named `connections` for that reason.

Two corrections it already carries: `-i any` captures the same packet on the veth, the gateway bridge AND the NIC, which would treble every count (deduped by source port); and an inbound visitor's ClientHello looks identical to ours, which had `muffin-grafana.rafiki.guru` filed as egress until the RFC1918 source filter went in.

panels.title: Egress connections — which container called which host
panels.description: The join the inference cannot make: openbb-api's own upstream calls, attributed. Source is the docker_gwbridge address, mapped to the swarm service via the container's SandboxID — `docker inspect` exposes only the overlay IP, so mapping that alone leaves every external connection labelled with a bare address.

panels.title: Egress collector — ClientHellos it could not parse
panels.description:
The SNI collector's own health signal, and until now nothing plotted it — so a collector silently failing to read the hostname out of every packet would have looked identical to a quiet network.

A non-zero rate is not automatically a fault: a TLS ClientHello can legitimately carry no `server_name` (an IP-literal connection has nothing to put there). A rate that RISES while `muffin_egress_connections_total` stays flat is the signature worth acting on — it means traffic is leaving that we can no longer attribute.
